sites.name: M/V HONDIUS
sites.desc: Dutch-flagged polar vessel arriving Granadilla cargo port 04:00–06:00 local 10 May. Will NOT pier-dock — passengers transferred by inflatable boats to isolated cordoned quayside, then guarded Spanish Army buses to airport by nationality. Disembarkation begins only once repatriation aircraft confirmed runway-ready. Oceanwide confirms all 147 aboard remain asymptomatic and PCR-negative as of 09 May. German woman's body still aboard. Weather window closes Tuesday; ship to proceed to Netherlands for decontamination post-disembarkation.

sites.name: USHUAIA / ARGENTINA ROUTE
sites.desc: Confirmed source investigation zone. Argentine Health Ministry 06 May report: Dutch index couple conducted 4-month birdwatching road trip (27 Nov 2025–01 Apr 2026) through Chile, Uruguay, and Argentina — crossing border with Chile multiple times via Neuquén and visiting Misiones, both WHO-designated Andes virus endemic zones. Ushuaia landfill now a specific investigation point: Dutch couple suspected exposed during birdwatching visit to site. Malbrán Institute to dispatch team to Ushuaia imminently; rodent trapping/testing along travel route active. Argentine national tally: 101 infections since Jun 2025.

sites.name: SAINT HELENA
sites.desc: 30 passengers disembarked 24 Apr (includes Dutch index male body and Dutch widow who later died in Johannesburg). Swiss confirmed male case also disembarked here. UKHSA contact-tracing 82 passengers + 6 crew from 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight ongoing. Disembarkees from 12 countries departed before hantavirus was confirmed (02 May). 7 UK nationals from St Helena disembarkation traced by UKHSA; 2 self-isolating in UK.

sites.name: JOHANNESBURG
sites.desc: Case 2 (Dutch widow, 69, PCR+) died at Johannesburg hospital 26 Apr — sole WHO-confirmed Andes virus death as of 09 May. Case 3 (British guide Martin Anstee, 56, PCR+) treated at Johannesburg ICU; condition improved and transferred to Netherlands. NICD contact-traced 65+ contacts from 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight (82 pax + 6 crew). Asymptomatic South African woman (briefly in Barcelona) confirmed located and monitored in South Africa.

sites.name: AMSTERDAM / NIJMEGEN
sites.desc: British Case 3 (Anstee, 56) transferred to Netherlands after condition improved. Dutch crew member (41, confirmed) treated at Radboud UMC Nijmegen. Netherlands lab PCR-confirmed postmortem that German woman died of Andes virus. KLM flight attendant tested NEGATIVE 08 May — not a secondary transmission case. GGD Kennemerland escalated KL592 monitoring to ALL passengers on flight (previously only rows near deceased). RIVM contact tracing ongoing.

sites.name: LONDON
sites.desc: UKHSA confirmed 2 British nationals PCR+ (one transferred to Netherlands, one treated South Africa) and flagged a 3rd suspected/probable case on Tristan da Cunha (08 May). UK repatriation flight arranged for 19 passengers and 4 crew from Tenerife; FCDO/UKHSA RDT pre-positioned. Returning asymptomatic Britons to isolate up to 45 days per UKHSA guidance.

sites.name: PARIS
sites.desc: Eight French nationals identified as close contacts of confirmed case on 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight — none were on the cruise. One reporting mild symptoms, isolated pending PCR results. French health ministry coordinating diagnostics and quarantine measures. Repatriation flight from Tenerife confirmed for French nationals aboard.

sites.name: ZURICH
sites.desc: PCR-confirmed male passenger disembarked St Helena 24 Apr via South Africa and Qatar; symptoms onset 01 May, tested positive Andes virus 05 May at University Hospital Zurich. Wife (also on trip) asymptomatic and isolating. Swiss authorities conducting additional contact tracing for anyone who had contact with patient after his return to Switzerland.

sites.name: BERLIN / DÜSSELDORF
sites.desc: German woman died on board 02 May (fever/malaise onset 28 Apr, developed pneumonia). Netherlands laboratory postmortem PCR returned Andes virus positive; cause of death still officially under investigation. Asymptomatic 65-year-old German contact evacuated 06 May to Netherlands, subsequently returned to Germany (Düsseldorf) for monitoring. RKI contact tracing active. Repatriation flight from Tenerife confirmed for German nationals aboard.

sites.name: ALICANTE
sites.desc: 32-year-old woman hospitalized in negative-pressure isolation with mild symptoms compatible with hantavirus; was on same 25 Apr St Helena–Johannesburg flight as deceased Dutch woman but seated two rows behind — classified lower risk. PCR results expected within 24 hours of 09 May; Health Secretary Padilla noted positive result is 'pretty unlikely.' If negative and asymptomatic, will transfer to Gómez Ulla for quarantine.

sites.name: TENERIFE
sites.desc: Hondius arriving Granadilla cargo port 04:00–06:00 local 10 May. Passengers evacuated by inflatable boats to isolated cordoned quayside; guarded Spanish Army buses to airport. Disembarkation by nationality only when respective repatriation aircraft confirmed runway-ready. WHO DG Tedros traveling personally to Tenerife to coordinate operation. Weather window closes Tuesday. La Candelaria University Hospital High-Level Isolation Unit (HCIU) activated as backup.

sites.name: MADRID
sites.desc: Gómez Ulla Military Hospital fully activated to receive 14 Spanish Hondius passengers; protocol covers all aboard 01 Apr–10 May or in close contact with confirmed case. PCR on arrival + Day 7; twice-daily temperature checks; single rooms, no visitors. Biosecurity equivalent to Ebola/COVID-19 protocols; 60–80 additional staff recruited. Alicante patient to transfer here if PCR-negative but still symptomatic.

sites.name: BARCELONA
sites.desc: Two Barcelona contacts now monitored: (1) South African woman (asymptomatic flight contact of Dutch deceased) spent ~1 week here before returning to South Africa — confirmed asymptomatic. (2) New 09 May: Barcelona-resident woman identified as flight contact after initially escaping detection due to mid-flight seat change; asymptomatic, now officially placed under monitoring and surveillance per Spanish Health Ministry.

sites.name: TRISTAN DA CUNHA
sites.desc: UKHSA flagged probable case (08 May): British male disembarked Hondius 13–15 Apr Tristan da Cunha stop; symptoms onset 28 Apr, currently stable in isolation on island. UKHSA assessing remotely. Spouse isolating as precaution. 6 additional guests had joined Hondius at Tristan da Cunha per Oceanwide, expanding contact tracing scope. Island population approximately 220 permanent residents.

sites.name: SINGAPORE
sites.desc: CLEARED 09 May: Both male residents (aged 67 and 65) tested NEGATIVE for hantavirus including Andes virus via multiple PCR samples — Singapore CDA confirmed. Both had disembarked Hondius at St Helena and traveled on 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight. Monitoring continues as precaution through incubation window.

sites.name: ONTARIO
sites.desc: Two Ontario residents self-isolating — Hondius passengers who returned home early, asymptomatic. Four Canadians total remain aboard vessel awaiting Tenerife evacuation. PHAC coordinating monitoring per 07 May government statement.

sites.name: QUEBEC
sites.desc: One Quebec resident self-isolating — not a Hondius passenger but shared homebound flight with two Canadian Hondius disembarkees. Asymptomatic; PHAC monitoring active.

sites.name: ARIZONA
sites.desc: ADHS monitoring one returning passenger under 42-day observation. Asymptomatic as of 09 May. CDC notified ADHS 05 May; public risk assessed as very low. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states.

sites.name: CALIFORNIA
sites.desc: CDPH monitoring one returned Hondius traveler via daily temperature checks and symptom assessment. A second California resident remains aboard ship and will transit Tenerife to Nebraska NQU via CDC-escorted State Dept charter. No California residents reported ill or infected as of 09 May.

sites.name: GEORGIA
sites.desc: Georgia DPH monitoring two residents who returned from Hondius. Both in good health with no signs of infection as of 08 May per GDPH statement. Following CDC recommendations. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort.

sites.name: TEXAS
sites.desc: Texas DSHS monitoring two returning Hondius passengers. Both asymptomatic. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states; none of the monitored US residents exhibiting signs of illness as of 09 May.

sites.name: VIRGINIA
sites.desc: VDH monitoring one returning Hondius passenger. Asymptomatic. CDC classified response as Level-3 (lowest emergency activation tier); Emergency Operations Center activated. Six states — AZ, CA, GA, TX, VA, NJ — monitoring at least 9 early-disembarkees or contacts per CDC/ABC 08–09 May reporting.

sites.name: NEW JERSEY
sites.desc: NJ health authorities monitoring two individuals with potential post-disembarkation exposure to a Hondius passenger. Neither symptomatic as of 09 May. Part of the broader US monitoring cohort per reporting.

sites.name: NEBRASKA
sites.desc: Nebraska Medicine / UNMC National Quarantine Unit (NQU) fully staffed and activated. CDC team pre-deployed to Offutt AFB, Bellevue. 17 American Hondius passengers (including one Utah resident) to arrive via CDC-escorted State Dept biocontainment charter from Tenerife. Dr. Wadman (NQU medical director) confirmed all 17 asymptomatic; anyone developing symptoms to be moved to Biocontainment Unit. Nebraska Medicine CEO Dr. Ash: 'We are prepared for situations exactly like this.'

sites.name: UTAH
sites.desc: Utah DHHS confirmed 08 May that at least one Utah resident is among the 17 Americans still aboard MV Hondius. Person is asymptomatic and will disembark in Tenerife, then travel with federal escort to Nebraska NQU for quarantine. No Utah residents monitored at home as of 09 May.

sites.name: MANILA
sites.desc: 38 Filipino crew members aboard Hondius; Philippines DOH confirmed none are currently ill as of 09 May. In close coordination with vessel operator and international authorities. Monitoring continues pending Tenerife disembarkation and subsequent repatriation.

sites.name: DUBLIN
sites.desc: Two Irish nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per RTE. Ireland is among nine EU/EEA nationalities on board per ECDC briefing. Repatriation flight from Tenerife confirmed for Irish nationals. Irish Dept of Health coordinating with ECDC and WHO; returning Irish nationals to quarantine per national protocol.

sites.name: PRAIA
sites.desc: Hondius anchored off Praia 03–06 May; departed 19:15 local 06 May for Tenerife. Three medevac patients evacuated here 06 May — two flew to Amsterdam (received by specialist teams at Schiphol), third plane made unscheduled refueling stop at Gran Canaria after Morocco refused permission and a medical equipment malfunction caused further delays. Cape Verde assessed unable to handle full passenger evacuation. 2,500 Argentine diagnostic kits dispatched to five countries.

sites.name: COPENHAGEN
sites.desc: Danish Patient Safety Authority confirmed 08 May that one Danish national was aboard MV Hondius. Person returned to Denmark end of April, is self-isolating, has displayed no symptoms, and was not in close contact with any confirmed cases. Monitoring active per national protocol.

sites.name: BRUSSELS
sites.desc: Belgian nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing (Belgium among nine EU/EEA nationalities on board). Repatriation flight from Tenerife confirmed. Belgian federal health authorities coordinating with ECDC. No symptomatic cases reported as of 09 May.

sites.name: WELLINGTON
sites.desc: New Zealand confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring nationals who had disembarked MV Hondius per WHO/CBS News 08 May. NZ Ministry of Health coordinating contact tracing; no symptomatic cases reported as of 09 May.

sites.name: STOCKHOLM
sites.desc: Sweden confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring nationals who had disembarked MV Hondius per WHO/CBS News 08 May. Swedish Public Health Agency (Folkhälsomyndigheten) coordinating; no symptomatic cases reported as of 09 May.

sites.name: ANKARA
sites.desc: Turkey confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring nationals who had disembarked MV Hondius per WHO/CBS News 08 May. Turkish Ministry of Health coordinating; no symptomatic cases reported as of 09 May.

sites.name: BASSETERRE
sites.desc: Saint Kitts and Nevis confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring nationals who had disembarked MV Hondius per WHO/CBS News 08 May. Local health authorities monitoring; no symptomatic cases reported as of 09 May.

sites.name: ATHENS
sites.desc: Greek nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing (Greece among nine EU/EEA nationalities on board). Greek Ministry of Health coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported as of 09 May. Monitoring of returning nationals underway.

sites.name: WARSAW
sites.desc: Polish nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing (Poland among nine EU/EEA nationalities on board). Polish Chief Sanitary Inspectorate coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported as of 09 May.

sites.name: LISBON
sites.desc: Portuguese nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing (Portugal among nine EU/EEA nationalities on board). DGS Portugal coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported as of 09 May.
